summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style entry on "I Hate This Part", a song by the American girl group The Pussycat Dolls from their second album, "Doll Domination" (2008). It covers the songwriters and producers, the song's origin as a track recorded for Nicole Scherzinger's cancelled solo project "Her Name Is Nicole", its single releases, and its musical style and lyrical theme. The song is described as a dance/R&B-influenced pop ballad about the conversation before a breakup.
one_line: "I Hate This Part" is a 2008 dance/R&B-influenced pop ballad by The Pussycat Dolls about the conversation before a breakup.
key_facts: "I Hate This Part" is a song by American girl group The Pussycat Dolls from their second album, "Doll Domination" (2008).
The song was written by Wayne Hector, Lucas Secon, Jonas Jeberg and Mich Hansen.
The song was produced by Jonas Jeberg and Mich Hansen, along with Ron Fair and Nicole Scherzinger.
The song was initially recorded for Nicole Scherzinger's planned solo project, "Her Name Is Nicole".
After the cancellation of "Her Name Is Nicole", the song was placed on the group's second album.
"I Hate This Part" was released on October 14, 2008 as the second international single.
"I Hate This Part" impacted contemporary hit radio stations on October 20, 2008 as the fourth single in the United States.
The single was released by Interscope Records.
"I Hate This Part" is a dance/R&B-influenced pop ballad.
The song ditches the Pussycat Dolls' usual sexual image in favor of introspection.
Lyrically, the song is about the conversation before a breakup.
